the diversity and materiality in cash-accrUAL adjustments to be made when reporting to Eurostat from cash-based GA to accrual-based National Accounts, raise concerns about the reliability of the final deficit/suplus reported by some EU member states.

GA budgetary balance should be reported on an accrual basis, as in NA, in order to achieve the reliability needed in the deficit/surpluses reported to Eurostat.

the accounting basis adopted in the budgetary reporting system has a material effect in the deficit/surpluses reliability, especially when the budgetary balance is still cash-based, as is still the case in several EU member states.

, when reporting to Eurostat, the EU countries should move to accrual-based GA and NA, and that the accounting basis differences between the two should be eliminated.

cash-accual adjustments are more material and diverse in countries still adopting GA cash-based budgetary accounting and, consequently, more relevant for deficit assessment and the reliability of reported deficit/surplus.
